ru: Любопы́тный ребёнок спра́шивал бы без конца́.
note: Imperfective бы with no protasis is a general hypothetical; the "would ask" collision is fixed on the perfective side («Ты бы спроси́ла…»).
"asking for directions" is the natural English for спра́шивать доро́гу.
Frame collision is with a perfective imperative, so the declarative "I ask passers-by" still cues the imperfective.
Imperfective imperative against a perfective one, but the objects and the conditional clause keep the two sentences distinct.

ru: На уро́ке учи́тель бу́дет спра́шивать ка́ждого.
en: In the lesson the teacher will be asking each one.
note: Imperfective compound future бу́дет спра́шивать was flattened to a bare "will ask", colliding with three спроси́ть futures; the progressive marks the repeated calling-on.
"often asked" already carries the habitual reading the imperfective needs, and the partner sentence shares no other wording.

ru: Ты бы спроси́ла об э́том у врача́.
en: You should ask a doctor about this.
note: «Ты бы + past» with no protasis is advisory rather than conditional, and the advisory reading also clears the "would ask" collision with спра́шивал бы.

ru: Я спрошу́ учи́теля об уро́ке за́втра.

note: спря́таны is a short passive participle; "are hidden" is exactly right, and "in the desk" is the natural English for keys in a стол.

en: I will hide the present in the cupboard.
note: шкаф is glossed "cupboard" and its twin sentence already says cupboard, so "wardrobe" is an unnecessary divergence from the tap-hint.

ru: Я спря́тала бы ключ в друго́м ме́сте.
note: No protasis, so this is a present counterfactual and "would hide" is correct; the partner sentence (a squirrel and nuts) carries its own cue.

ru: Я спря́чу пода́рок в шкаф за́втра.
В пеще́ру мы бу́дем спуска́ться по верёвке.
en: We will be descending into the cave using a rope.
note: Imperfective бу́дем спуска́ться flattened to "will descend", which collides with the perfective «Тума́н спусти́тся к ве́черу»; the progressive is the aspect cue.

ru: Без верёвки я бы не спуска́лся туда́.
note: Imperfective conditional is right as it stands; the perfective partner takes the "would have" reading instead.

ru: Ско́ро я спущу́сь на пе́рвый эта́ж.
Я спущу́сь в подва́л за ва́реньем.
Без ли́фта я бы спусти́лась по ле́стнице.
en: Without a lift I would have descended by the stairs.
note: Perfective бы+past against an imperfective partner with the same "would descend" frame; the completed single descent reads "would have descended".

ru: Пока́ мы бу́дем ста́вить пала́тку, де́ти бу́дут игра́ть у воды́.
note: No aspect collision here, and "While we put up the tent" is the ordinary English for a Russian future subordinate clause.

ru: Я ста́вила бы кни́ги по поря́дку.
Без со́лнца дни станови́лись бы мрачне́е.
en: Without the sun the days would be getting gloomier.
note: станови́лись бы is the gradual process, and every other станови́ться example here uses "getting"; this also clears the "would become" collision with стал бы.

ru: На экза́мене я бу́ду стара́ться и́зо всех сил.
en: In the exam I will be trying with all my might.
note: Imperfective бу́ду стара́ться flattened to "will try" collides with three постара́ться futures at once; "will be trying" is natural and aspect-marked.

ru: Я стара́лась бы ещё бо́льше ра́ди тебя́.
note: The imperfective reads correctly; the colliding "would try" belongs to постара́ться, which is outside this packet.

en: They were trying hard not to make noise.
note: Imperfective past of sustained effort, and the simple past "tried hard" is already the perfective partner's rendering.
Collision partner is a perfective imperative, so the declarative first person still distinguishes the two.

ru: Е́сли бы мог, я стал бы учи́телем.
Без трениро́вок он бы не стал чемпио́ном.
note: Perfective бы+past with a counterfactual protasis, already rendered "would not have become".
The English dropped оде́жду entirely; the sibling sentence already renders стира́ть оде́жду as "washes clothes".

ru: В друго́м магази́не пла́тье сто́ило бы деше́вле.
За́втра э́тот това́р бу́дет сто́ить доро́же.
note: "will be costing" is not English, so the flat future stays; сто́ить is stative and has no aspect partner to collide with.
"cost a fair bit" renders the litotes недёшево while keeping the headword verb, which a bare "are not cheap" would lose.

ru: Перед конце́ртом посети́тели бу́дут стоя́ть в о́череди.
en: Before the concert visitors will be standing in a queue.
note: "will queue" collapses бу́дут стоя́ть в о́череди and loses the headword стоя́ть along with the compound future.

ru: Сто́я в о́череди, он чита́л газе́ту.
Без подде́ржки стена́ не стоя́ла бы до́лго.

note: "will be suffering" would be unnatural in a generic conditional, so the flat future is correct here.

ru: Без лека́рства он страда́л бы от бо́ли.

en: The workers were building the bridge for two years.
note: "built the bridge for two years" is not idiomatic English for a durative imperfective past; the progressive is both natural and aspect-correct.
стро́ить пла́ны is an idiom; "make plans" is the English idiom and "build plans" is not English.

ru: С деньга́ми я бы стро́ил большо́й дом.
note: The imperfective reads correctly; the "would build" collision is with постро́ить, outside this packet.

ru: Ско́ро они́ бу́дут стро́ить но́вую шко́лу.
Я стучу́, но никто́ не отвеча́ет.

note: "knocking on the roof" keeps the headword literal and is still readable English.
General imperfective hypothetical; the colliding "would knock" belongs to постуча́ть, outside this packet.

ru: Че́рез мину́ту он бу́дет стуча́ть в дверь.

note: Idiomatic rendering of «Су́дя по всему́»; note this Russian sentence appears twice in the corpus with two different English renderings.
Literal rendering of the same Russian sentence that also appears above with "By all appearances"; both are accurate.

ru: За́втра он бу́дет суди́ть фина́льный матч.
note: "referee" is the standard sense of суди́ть with a match, and the compound future is already progressive.

ru: Он су́дит о́бо всём сли́шком стро́го.
Я не суди́ла бы люде́й так стро́го.
Е́сли б знал, я суме́л бы помо́чь.
note: Perfective бы+past with a past protasis, correctly rendered "would have managed".

en: He shoved the note into his pocket.
note: The tap-hint for су́нул reads "to shove", which the four sibling sentences use; "stuck" is a needless divergence here.

ru: Ско́ро я су́ну письмо́ в я́щик.
Я су́нул бы запи́ску под дверь.

note: "will be existing" is not English, so the flat future is right.
Russian present + давно́ maps to the English present perfect; that is the correct rendering, not a padding defect.

ru: Без во́здуха жизнь не существова́ла бы.
Я схвачу́ его́ за́ руку за́втра.
Я схвати́л бы су́мку и убежа́л.
note: No protasis and no collision, so the present-counterfactual "would seize" stands.

ru: По́сле вы́боров мы бу́дем счита́ть голоса́ всю ночь.

note: Identical English to the ты variant is expected here; phraseAmbiguity supplies the ты/вы note.
Identical English to the вы variant is expected here; phraseAmbiguity supplies the ты/вы note.

ru: Е́сли бы бы́ло вре́мя, я сшил бы су́мку.
note: Perfective бы+past with a past protasis, correctly rendered "would have sewn".

ru: Я сошью́ што́ры из э́той тка́ни.

note: The "will eat up" rendering already distinguishes this from the imperfective есть future.

ru: Я съе́ла бы ещё кусо́чек то́рта.
note: "eat up another little piece" keeps the perfective marker; the reading is clear and no partner collides with it.
